title: Theory of the $1/9$ Magnetization Plateau of the Spin-$1/2$ Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet
abstract: We investigate the $1/9$ magnetization plateau of the spin-$1/2$ kagome Heisenberg antiferromagnet using infinite projected entangled-pair states and identify a spin-density-wave state with a $27$-site unit cell and a lower variational energy than previous approaches. In contrast to higher-magnetization plateaus, which are well described by localized magnons on nonoverlapping hexagons and preserve a sixfold rotational symmetry, the $1/9$ plateau only keeps a threefold rotational symmmetry and consists of a tiling by three types of $9$-site clusters related by $\pm2π/3$ rotations. These conclusions are supported by a complementary cluster mean-field theory which correctly preserves the symmetry of the higher plateaus but leads to the same spontaneous symmetry breaking for the $1/9$ plateau with a qualitatively similar pattern of nine different local magnetizations.
summary: This work theoretically characterizes the 1/9 magnetization plateau in the Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet, proposing a Spin-Density-Wave (SDW) state with a 27-site unit cell. Using iPEPS and CMFT, the authors demonstrate that this plateau breaks the system's sixfold rotational symmetry, a key distinction from other magnetization plateaus. The findings advance the understanding of quantum magnetism in highly frustrated lattices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the microscopic nature and symmetry properties of the low-field 1/9 magnetization plateau in the spin-1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet.
main_result: The 1/9 plateau is identified as a Spin-Density-Wave (SDW) state characterized by a 27-site unit cell, which spontaneously breaks the system's sixfold rotational symmetry down to threefold symmetry.
method: The study employs advanced quantum many-body techniques, including Infinite Projected Entangled-Pair States (iPEPS) and Cluster Mean-Field Theory (CMFT), supplemented by Exact Diagonalization (ED) on finite clusters.
model_or_system: The system is the spin-1/2 Kagome Heisenberg Antiferromagnet, modeled by a Hamiltonian subjected to an external magnetic field (Zeeman term). The analysis focuses on the magnetization curve $m/m_s$ as a function of the field $h$.
key_observables: Magnetization ($m/m_s$), variational energy per site $e(m)$, local magnetizations, and nearest-neighbor spin-spin correlations.
important_parameters: The magnetic field $h$ (specifically in the range $h \in (0.2, 0.46)$ for the plateau), and the bond dimension $D$ used in the tensor network calculations.
main_assumptions: The primary approximations involve using the iPEPS ansatz with a simple update scheme and exploiting the approximate threefold rotational symmetry to reduce the unit cell size for computational feasibility.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the magnetization plateau region, the convergence of variational energy with bond dimension, and real-space patterns of local magnetizations and correlations confirming the SDW structure.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the physical problem, applying iPEPS/CMFT to find the 27-site SDW structure, and then contrasting this symmetry breaking pattern with the higher-magnetization plateaus which retain higher symmetry.
why_interesting: The detailed analysis of symmetry breaking in quantum magnetic materials using tensor networks provides a rigorous theoretical framework for understanding exotic quantum phases in frustrated lattice models.

The magnetization increases continuously from zero at zero field and attains the 1/9 plateau at h ≃0.2. This plateau persists up to h ≃0.46, after which the magnetization rises toward the 1/3 plateau, with a subtle feature near m/ms = 5/27.
